'''Michel Enock-Levi''' (1 June 1947 – 5 June 2025) was a French mathematician and a {{ill|Directeur de recherche au CNRS|fr|lt=research director at CNRS}},<ref name="file">{{cite web | url = https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.enock/Site/Fiche%20personnelle.html | language = fr | title = Michel Enock - personal file | publisher = Institute of Mathematics at University Jussieu-Paris Left Bank | access-date = September 9, 2023}}</ref> credited with the early development of [[Pontryagin duality#Dualities for non-commutative topological groups|Pontryagin-style dualities for non-commutative topological groups]]. Enock died in June 2025, at the age of 78.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://smf.emath.fr/actualites-smf/deces-de-michel-enock|title=Décès de Michel Enock &#124| publisher = Société Mathématique de France|website=smf.emath.fr | first = Christian | last  =Peskine |date = June 6, 2025}}</ref>

== Scientific contributions ==
Enock is known for the 1992 book co-authored with Jean-Marie Schwartz on the subject of Kac algebras,<ref name="book">{{cite book |last1=Enock|first1=Michel|last2=Schwartz|first2=Jean-Marie|title=Kac Algebras and Duality of Locally Compact Groups|year=1992|publisher=Springer-Verlag|isbn=978-3-540-54745-7| others=With a preface by Alain Connes. With a postface by Adrian Ocneanu| location= Berlin|mr=1215933|doi=10.1007/978-3-662-02813-1}}</ref> (not to be confused with [[Kac-Moody algebras]]). According to the French mathematician [[Alain Connes]],<ref>{{cite book | url = https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-662-02813-1#about-this-book| first = Alain | last = Connes | title = Preface to the book 'Kac algebras' | year=1992 | publisher = Springer| doi = 10.1007/978-3-662-02813-1 | isbn = 978-3-642-08128-6 }}</ref> the book develops the general theory to characterize [[quantum groups]] among [[Hopf algebras]], similar to the characterization of [[Lie groups]] among [[locally compact group]]s, "with emphasis on the analytical aspects of the subject instead of the purely algebraic ones". Further, Connes writes: {{cquote|The theory of Kac algebras and their duality, [was] elaborated independently by M. Enock and J. -M. Schwartz, and by G. I. Kac and [[Leonid I. Vainerman|L. I. Vainermann]] in the seventies. The subject has now reached a state of maturity }}
Specifically, Enock co-developed a general [[Pontryagin duality]] theory for all [[locally compact group]]s.

== Scientific career ==
Enock completed his postgraduate thesis (1971) and state thesis (1976) at [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]]. In 1971, he became an assistant professor at the University of Paris 13 ([[Sorbonne Paris North University]]). From 1978, he was a Researcher at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS). He received accreditation to direct research at [[Paris Diderot University]] in 1985. He supervised two doctorate students.<ref name="MGP">{{cite web |title=Profile of Michel Enock (ID 294851) |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=294851 |website=The Mathematics Genealogy Project |publisher=North Dakota State University, Dept. of Mathematics, in association with the American Mathematical Society |access-date=2025-07-25}}</ref>

Enock became a Director of Research at CNRS in 2000 and a First class Research Director in 2011. From 2012, he was emeritus Research Director at CNRS.<ref name="file"/>
